opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_kms_cmk_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption (SSE-KMS)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration"
  not r.change.after.apply_server_side_encryption_by_default
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure apply_server_side_encryption_by_default.sse_algorithm for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_block_public_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3 Block Public Access Across All Dimensions
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block"
  not r.change.after.block_public_acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure block_public_acls for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_secure_transport_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Transport Encryption via aws:SecureTransport
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.condition.aws_secure_transport for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_versioning_mfa_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable S3 Versioning and MFA Delete Protection
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_versioning"
  not r.change.after.versioning_configuration
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure versioning_configuration.status for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_access_logging_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Server Access Logging to Central Log Archive
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_logging"
  not r.change.after.target_bucket
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure target_bucket for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_object_lock_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3 Object Lock Compliance Mode Retention (WORM)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration"
  not r.change.after.object_lock_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure object_lock_enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_replication_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Cross-Region Bi-Directional Replication (CRR)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration"
  not r.change.after.role
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure role for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_bucket_key_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable S3 Bucket Key to Reduce KMS Cryptographic Overhead
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration"
  not r.change.after.bucket_key_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure bucket_key_enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_lifecycle_mpu_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Lifecycle Expiration for Incomplete Multipart Uploads
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration"
  not r.change.after.abort_incomplete_multipart_upload
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure abort_incomplete_multipart_upload for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_kms_cmk_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption (SSE-KMS) (Tier-2 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration"
  not r.change.after.apply_server_side_encryption_by_default
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure apply_server_side_encryption_by_default.sse_algorithm for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_block_public_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3 Block Public Access Across All Dimensions (Tier-2 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block"
  not r.change.after.block_public_acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure block_public_acls for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_secure_transport_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Transport Encryption via aws:SecureTransport (Tier-2 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.condition.aws_secure_transport for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_versioning_mfa_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable S3 Versioning and MFA Delete Protection (Tier-2 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_versioning"
  not r.change.after.versioning_configuration
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure versioning_configuration.status for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_access_logging_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Server Access Logging to Central Log Archive (Tier-2 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_logging"
  not r.change.after.target_bucket
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure target_bucket for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_object_lock_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3 Object Lock Compliance Mode Retention (WORM) (Tier-2 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration"
  not r.change.after.object_lock_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure object_lock_enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_replication_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Cross-Region Bi-Directional Replication (CRR) (Tier-2 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration"
  not r.change.after.role
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure role for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_bucket_key_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable S3 Bucket Key to Reduce KMS Cryptographic Overhead (Tier-2 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration"
  not r.change.after.bucket_key_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure bucket_key_enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_lifecycle_mpu_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Lifecycle Expiration for Incomplete Multipart Uploads (Tier-2 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration"
  not r.change.after.abort_incomplete_multipart_upload
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure abort_incomplete_multipart_upload for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_kms_cmk_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption (SSE-KMS) (Tier-3 • Profile S)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration"
  not r.change.after.apply_server_side_encryption_by_default
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure apply_server_side_encryption_by_default.sse_algorithm for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_block_public_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3 Block Public Access Across All Dimensions (Tier-3 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block"
  not r.change.after.block_public_acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure block_public_acls for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_secure_transport_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Transport Encryption via aws:SecureTransport (Tier-3 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.condition.aws_secure_transport for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_versioning_mfa_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable S3 Versioning and MFA Delete Protection (Tier-3 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_versioning"
  not r.change.after.versioning_configuration
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure versioning_configuration.status for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_access_logging_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Server Access Logging to Central Log Archive (Tier-3 • Profile W)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_logging"
  not r.change.after.target_bucket
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure target_bucket for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_object_lock_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3 Object Lock Compliance Mode Retention (WORM) (Tier-3 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration"
  not r.change.after.object_lock_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure object_lock_enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_replication_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Cross-Region Bi-Directional Replication (CRR) (Tier-3 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration"
  not r.change.after.role
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure role for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_bucket_key_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable S3 Bucket Key to Reduce KMS Cryptographic Overhead (Tier-3 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration"
  not r.change.after.bucket_key_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure bucket_key_enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_lifecycle_mpu_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Lifecycle Expiration for Incomplete Multipart Uploads (Tier-3 • Profile A)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration"
  not r.change.after.abort_incomplete_multipart_upload
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure abort_incomplete_multipart_upload for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_kms_cmk_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption (SSE-KMS) (Tier-4 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration"
  not r.change.after.apply_server_side_encryption_by_default
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure apply_server_side_encryption_by_default.sse_algorithm for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_block_public_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3 Block Public Access Across All Dimensions (Tier-4 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block"
  not r.change.after.block_public_acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure block_public_acls for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_secure_transport_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Transport Encryption via aws:SecureTransport (Tier-4 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.condition.aws_secure_transport for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_versioning_mfa_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable S3 Versioning and MFA Delete Protection (Tier-4 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_versioning"
  not r.change.after.versioning_configuration
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure versioning_configuration.status for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_access_logging_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Server Access Logging to Central Log Archive (Tier-4 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_logging"
  not r.change.after.target_bucket
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure target_bucket for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_object_lock_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3 Object Lock Compliance Mode Retention (WORM) (Tier-4 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration"
  not r.change.after.object_lock_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure object_lock_enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_replication_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Cross-Region Bi-Directional Replication (CRR) (Tier-4 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration"
  not r.change.after.role
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure role for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_bucket_key_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable S3 Bucket Key to Reduce KMS Cryptographic Overhead (Tier-4 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration"
  not r.change.after.bucket_key_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure bucket_key_enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_lifecycle_mpu_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure S3 Lifecycle Expiration for Incomplete Multipart Uploads (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration"
  not r.change.after.abort_incomplete_multipart_upload
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure abort_incomplete_multipart_upload for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_kms_cmk_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption (SSE-KMS) (Tier-5 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration"
  not r.change.after.apply_server_side_encryption_by_default
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure apply_server_side_encryption_by_default.sse_algorithm for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_block_public_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce S3 Block Public Access Across All Dimensions (Tier-5 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block"
  not r.change.after.block_public_acls
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure block_public_acls for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.storage_s3.storage_s3_s3_secure_transport_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Transport Encryption via aws:SecureTransport (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_s3_bucket_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.condition.aws_secure_transport for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
