developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_trust_policy_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict AssumeRole Trust Policy to Explicit Principal Arns (Tier-5 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_role"
  not r.change.after.assume_role_policy
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure assume_role_policy for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      requirement --> check

    end

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_abac_tags_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IAM Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) Tag Policies (Tier-5 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_policy"
  not r.change.after.policy_abac_tags
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure policy_abac_tags for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

      resource@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "AWS IAM", h: 64, pos: "b" }

    end

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_user_mfa_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for All Interactive IAM Users (Tier-6 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_user_policy_attachment"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enforced for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "AWS IAM", h: 64, pos: "b" }

    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_root_keys_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Root Account Access Keys and Inactive Console Credentials (Tier-6 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_access_key"
  not r.change.after.user
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure user for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.

opa_policy:
package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_key_rotation_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Automatic 90-Day Rotation for Programmatic Access Keys (Tier-6 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_access_key"
  not r.change.after.max_age_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure max_age_days for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.

package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_permission_boundary_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Permission Boundaries on All IAM Roles and Delegated Admins (Tier-6 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_role"
  not r.change.after.permissions_boundary
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure permissions_boundary for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.

package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_access_analyzer_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable IAM Access Analyzer for Continuous Cross-Account Detection (Tier-6 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_accessanalyzer_analyzer"
  not r.change.after.type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure type for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_trust_policy_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Restrict AssumeRole Trust Policy to Explicit Principal Arns (Tier-6 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_role"
  not r.change.after.assume_role_policy
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure assume_role_policy for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_abac_tags_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IAM Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) Tag Policies (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_policy"
  not r.change.after.policy_abac_tags
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure policy_abac_tags for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

    end

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.iam_access.iam_access_iam_user_mfa_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for All Interactive IAM Users (Tier-7 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_user_policy_attachment"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enforced
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enforced for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      change --> requirement

    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

      resource@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "AWS IAM", h: 64, pos: "b" }

    end

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.

opa_policy:
package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_flow_logs_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable VPC Flow Logs to Centralized Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_flow_log"
  not r.change.after.traffic_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure traffic_type for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_sg_no_open_admin_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Inbound 0.0.0.0/0 on Sensitive Administrative Ports
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_security_group_rule"
  not r.change.after.cidr_blocks
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cidr_blocks for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

# Rule: Deploy VPC PrivateLink Interface Endpoints for AWS Service Isolation
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_vpc_endpoint"
  not r.change.after.vpc_endpoint_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_endpoint_type for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_network_firewall_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy AWS Network Firewall with Stateful Suricata Rule Sets
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_networkfirewall_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_policy_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_policy_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_default_sg_closed_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default Security Group Complete Traffic Deny and Isolation
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_default_security_group"
  not r.change.after.ingress_egress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ingress_egress for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_flow_logs_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable VPC Flow Logs to Centralized Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_flow_log"
  not r.change.after.traffic_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure traffic_type for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_sg_no_open_admin_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Inbound 0.0.0.0/0 on Sensitive Administrative Ports (Tier-2 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_security_group_rule"
  not r.change.after.cidr_blocks
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cidr_blocks for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_privatelink_endpoints_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy VPC PrivateLink Interface Endpoints for AWS Service Isolation (Tier-2 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_vpc_endpoint"
  not r.change.after.vpc_endpoint_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_endpoint_type for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_network_firewall_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy AWS Network Firewall with Stateful Suricata Rule Sets (Tier-2 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_networkfirewall_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_policy_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_policy_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_default_sg_closed_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default Security Group Complete Traffic Deny and Isolation (Tier-2 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_default_security_group"
  not r.change.after.ingress_egress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ingress_egress for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_flow_logs_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable VPC Flow Logs to Centralized Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-3 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_flow_log"
  not r.change.after.traffic_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure traffic_type for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_sg_no_open_admin_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Inbound 0.0.0.0/0 on Sensitive Administrative Ports (Tier-3 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_security_group_rule"
  not r.change.after.cidr_blocks
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cidr_blocks for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_privatelink_endpoints_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy VPC PrivateLink Interface Endpoints for AWS Service Isolation (Tier-3 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_vpc_endpoint"
  not r.change.after.vpc_endpoint_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_endpoint_type for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_network_firewall_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy AWS Network Firewall with Stateful Suricata Rule Sets (Tier-3 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_networkfirewall_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_policy_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_policy_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_default_sg_closed_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default Security Group Complete Traffic Deny and Isolation (Tier-3 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_default_security_group"
  not r.change.after.ingress_egress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ingress_egress for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_flow_logs_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable VPC Flow Logs to Centralized Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-4 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_flow_log"
  not r.change.after.traffic_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure traffic_type for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_sg_no_open_admin_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Inbound 0.0.0.0/0 on Sensitive Administrative Ports (Tier-4 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_security_group_rule"
  not r.change.after.cidr_blocks
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cidr_blocks for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_privatelink_endpoints_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy VPC PrivateLink Interface Endpoints for AWS Service Isolation (Tier-4 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_vpc_endpoint"
  not r.change.after.vpc_endpoint_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_endpoint_type for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_network_firewall_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy AWS Network Firewall with Stateful Suricata Rule Sets (Tier-4 • Profile S)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_networkfirewall_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_policy_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_policy_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_default_sg_closed_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default Security Group Complete Traffic Deny and Isolation (Tier-4 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_default_security_group"
  not r.change.after.ingress_egress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ingress_egress for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:network-vpc", label: "Amazon VPC", h: 64, pos: "b" }

    end

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_flow_logs_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable VPC Flow Logs to Centralized Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-5 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_flow_log"
  not r.change.after.traffic_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure traffic_type for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_sg_no_open_admin_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Inbound 0.0.0.0/0 on Sensitive Administrative Ports (Tier-5 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_security_group_rule"
  not r.change.after.cidr_blocks
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cidr_blocks for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_privatelink_endpoints_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy VPC PrivateLink Interface Endpoints for AWS Service Isolation (Tier-5 • Profile W)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_vpc_endpoint"
  not r.change.after.vpc_endpoint_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_endpoint_type for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_network_firewall_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy AWS Network Firewall with Stateful Suricata Rule Sets (Tier-5 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_networkfirewall_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_policy_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_policy_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_default_sg_closed_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default Security Group Complete Traffic Deny and Isolation (Tier-5 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_default_security_group"
  not r.change.after.ingress_egress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ingress_egress for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_flow_logs_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable VPC Flow Logs to Centralized Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-6 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_flow_log"
  not r.change.after.traffic_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure traffic_type for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_sg_no_open_admin_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Inbound 0.0.0.0/0 on Sensitive Administrative Ports (Tier-6 • Profile A)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_security_group_rule"
  not r.change.after.cidr_blocks
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure cidr_blocks for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_privatelink_endpoints_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy VPC PrivateLink Interface Endpoints for AWS Service Isolation (Tier-6 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_vpc_endpoint"
  not r.change.after.vpc_endpoint_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_endpoint_type for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_network_firewall_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy AWS Network Firewall with Stateful Suricata Rule Sets (Tier-6 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_networkfirewall_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_policy_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure firewall_policy_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.network_vpc.network_vpc_vpc_default_sg_closed_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default Security Group Complete Traffic Deny and Isolation (Tier-6 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_default_security_group"
  not r.change.after.ingress_egress
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ingress_egress for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0116"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:network-vpc", label: "Amazon VPC", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.
