      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0151"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:compute-ec2", label: "Amazon EC2", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_no_public_ip_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Public IPv4 Addresses on Production Workload Instances (Tier-5 • Profile W)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_instance"
  not r.change.after.associate_public_ip_address
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure associate_public_ip_address for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ssm_agent_role_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Core Profile for Zero Open SSH Ports (Tier-5 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_instance_profile"
  not r.change.after.role
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure role for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

flowchart TB

      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0153"]
      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:compute-ec2", label: "Amazon EC2", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ebs_encryption_by_default_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default EBS Encryption Across All Regions in the Account (Tier-5 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_ebs_encryption_by_default"
  not r.change.after.enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_imdsv2_required_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IMDSv2 (HttpTokens=Required) to Prevent SSRF Credential Theft (Tier-6 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_instance"
  not r.change.after.metadata_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure metadata_options.http_tokens for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ebs_kms_encryption_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption on All Attached EBS Volumes (Tier-6 • Profile A)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_ebs_volume"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:compute-ec2", label: "Amazon EC2", h: 64, pos: "b" }

    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_no_public_ip_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Public IPv4 Addresses on Production Workload Instances (Tier-6 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_instance"
  not r.change.after.associate_public_ip_address
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure associate_public_ip_address for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ssm_agent_role_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Core Profile for Zero Open SSH Ports (Tier-6 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_instance_profile"
  not r.change.after.role
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure role for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      requirement --> check

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ebs_encryption_by_default_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default EBS Encryption Across All Regions in the Account (Tier-6 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_ebs_encryption_by_default"
  not r.change.after.enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_imdsv2_required_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IMDSv2 (HttpTokens=Required) to Prevent SSRF Credential Theft (Tier-7 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_instance"
  not r.change.after.metadata_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure metadata_options.http_tokens for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ebs_kms_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption on All Attached EBS Volumes (Tier-7 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_ebs_volume"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      change --> requirement

    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

      resource@{ icon: "logos:compute-ec2", label: "Amazon EC2", h: 64, pos: "b" }

    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_no_public_ip_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Public IPv4 Addresses on Production Workload Instances (Tier-7 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_instance"
  not r.change.after.associate_public_ip_address
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure associate_public_ip_address for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ssm_agent_role_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Core Profile for Zero Open SSH Ports (Tier-7 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_instance_profile"
  not r.change.after.role
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure role for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

flowchart TB

      change["Proposed configuration for Amazon EC2"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0163"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:compute-ec2", label: "Amazon EC2", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ebs_encryption_by_default_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default EBS Encryption Across All Regions in the Account (Tier-7 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_ebs_encryption_by_default"
  not r.change.after.enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_imdsv2_required_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IMDSv2 (HttpTokens=Required) to Prevent SSRF Credential Theft (Tier-8 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_instance"
  not r.change.after.metadata_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure metadata_options.http_tokens for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ebs_kms_encryption_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption on All Attached EBS Volumes (Tier-8 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_ebs_volume"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_no_public_ip_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Public IPv4 Addresses on Production Workload Instances (Tier-8 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_instance"
  not r.change.after.associate_public_ip_address
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure associate_public_ip_address for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ssm_agent_role_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Core Profile for Zero Open SSH Ports (Tier-8 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_iam_instance_profile"
  not r.change.after.role
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure role for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:compute-ec2", label: "Amazon EC2", h: 64, pos: "b" }

    end

      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ebs_encryption_by_default_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Default EBS Encryption Across All Regions in the Account (Tier-8 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_ebs_encryption_by_default"
  not r.change.after.enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_imdsv2_required_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce IMDSv2 (HttpTokens=Required) to Prevent SSRF Credential Theft (Tier-9 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_instance"
  not r.change.after.metadata_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure metadata_options.http_tokens for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_ebs_kms_encryption_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption on All Attached EBS Volumes (Tier-9 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_ebs_volume"
  not r.change.after.encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypted for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.compute_ec2.compute_ec2_ec2_no_public_ip_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Public IPv4 Addresses on Production Workload Instances (Tier-9 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_instance"
  not r.change.after.associate_public_ip_address
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure associate_public_ip_address for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_multi_az_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-AZ High Availability Deployment for Automatic Failover
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_db_instance"
  not r.change.after.multi_az
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure multi_az for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_storage_kms_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_db_instance"
  not r.change.after.storage_encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure storage_encrypted for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_no_public_access_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Public Accessibility on Database Subnets and Instances
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_db_instance"
  not r.change.after.publicly_accessible
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure publicly_accessible for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_activity_streams_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Database Activity Streams (DAS) for Asynchronous Auditing
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_rds_cluster_activity_stream"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_secrets_manager_rotation_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Automated Password Rotation via AWS Secrets Manager
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation"
  not r.change.after.rotation_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure rotation_days for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_multi_az_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-AZ High Availability Deployment for Automatic Failover (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_db_instance"
  not r.change.after.multi_az
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure multi_az for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_storage_kms_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest (Tier-2 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_db_instance"
  not r.change.after.storage_encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure storage_encrypted for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_no_public_access_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Public Accessibility on Database Subnets and Instances (Tier-2 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_db_instance"
  not r.change.after.publicly_accessible
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure publicly_accessible for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_activity_streams_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Database Activity Streams (DAS) for Asynchronous Auditing (Tier-2 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_rds_cluster_activity_stream"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_secrets_manager_rotation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Automated Password Rotation via AWS Secrets Manager (Tier-2 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation"
  not r.change.after.rotation_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure rotation_days for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.

failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_multi_az_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-AZ High Availability Deployment for Automatic Failover (Tier-3 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_db_instance"
  not r.change.after.multi_az
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure multi_az for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_storage_kms_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest (Tier-3 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_db_instance"
  not r.change.after.storage_encrypted
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure storage_encrypted for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.

failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_no_public_access_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Eliminate Public Accessibility on Database Subnets and Instances (Tier-3 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_db_instance"
  not r.change.after.publicly_accessible
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure publicly_accessible for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

package aws.database_rds.database_rds_rds_activity_streams_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Database Activity Streams (DAS) for Asynchronous Auditing (Tier-3 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_rds_cluster_activity_stream"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
