developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_dlq_configured_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Asynchronous Invocation Failures (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.target_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_in_vpc_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Lambda Functions inside Private VPC Subnets with Security Groups (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.vpc_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_config.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_env_kms_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Key for Environment Variables Encryption (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_dlq_configured_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Asynchronous Invocation Failures (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.target_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["AWS: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for AWS Lambda"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0371"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:serverless-lambda", label: "AWS Lambda", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_in_vpc_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Lambda Functions inside Private VPC Subnets with Security Groups (Tier-10 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.vpc_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_config.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_env_kms_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Key for Environment Variables Encryption (Tier-10 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["AWS: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for AWS Lambda"]
      requirement["Enforce Customer Managed KMS Key for Environment Variables Encryption"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0373"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:serverless-lambda", label: "AWS Lambda", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_dlq_configured_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Asynchronous Invocation Failures (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.target_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_in_vpc_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Lambda Functions inside Private VPC Subnets with Security Groups (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.vpc_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_config.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_env_kms_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Key for Environment Variables Encryption (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_dlq_configured_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Asynchronous Invocation Failures (Tier-11 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.target_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_in_vpc_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Lambda Functions inside Private VPC Subnets with Security Groups (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.vpc_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_config.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_env_kms_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Key for Environment Variables Encryption (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_dlq_configured_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Asynchronous Invocation Failures (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.target_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

flowchart TB

      change["Proposed configuration for AWS Lambda"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0380"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:serverless-lambda", label: "AWS Lambda", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_in_vpc_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Lambda Functions inside Private VPC Subnets with Security Groups (Tier-13 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.vpc_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_config.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_env_kms_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Key for Environment Variables Encryption (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["AWS: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for AWS Lambda"]
      requirement["Enforce Customer Managed KMS Key for Environment Variables Encryption"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0382"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:serverless-lambda", label: "AWS Lambda", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_dlq_configured_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Asynchronous Invocation Failures (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.target_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_in_vpc_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Lambda Functions inside Private VPC Subnets with Security Groups (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.vpc_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_config.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_env_kms_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Key for Environment Variables Encryption (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_dlq_configured_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Asynchronous Invocation Failures (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.target_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.serverless_lambda.serverless_lambda_lambda_in_vpc_t15

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Lambda Functions inside Private VPC Subnets with Security Groups (Tier-15 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_lambda_function"
  not r.change.after.vpc_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_config.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.

failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["AWS: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Amazon API Gateway"]
      requirement["Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0394"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:perimeter-apigateway", label: "Amazon API Gateway", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["AWS: proposed control change"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0400"]
      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:perimeter-apigateway", label: "Amazon API Gateway", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0403"]
      requirement --> check

    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:perimeter-apigateway", label: "Amazon API Gateway", h: 64, pos: "b" }

    end

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
