package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-7 • Profile S)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-7 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["AWS: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Amazon API Gateway"]
      requirement["Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0409"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:perimeter-apigateway", label: "Amazon API Gateway", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.

failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-10 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-10 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["AWS: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Amazon API Gateway"]
      requirement["Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0418"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:perimeter-apigateway", label: "Amazon API Gateway", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-11 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-13 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-0427"]
      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:perimeter-apigateway", label: "Amazon API Gateway", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_mtls_enforced_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Mutual TLS (mTLS) Authentication for Enterprise B2B APIs (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_domain_name"
  not r.change.after.mutual_tls_authentication
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mutual_tls_authentication for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_access_logging_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Detailed Access Logging to Encrypted CloudWatch Log Group (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_api_gateway_stage"
  not r.change.after.access_log_settings
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_log_settings.destination_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.

failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

package aws.perimeter_apigateway.perimeter_apigateway_apigw_waf_association_t15

default allow = false

# Rule: Associate AWS WAF WebACL to Protect Against Layer 7 Exploits (Tier-15 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association"
  not r.change.after.resource_arn
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure resource_arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Synchronous API request handling
developer_guide.contract: HTTP method, route, request schema, auth context and response status
dependencies: A deployed handler or container and an HTTP route
An invocation identity and downstream SDK permissions
steps: Implement schema validation and authorization in the handler.
Configure the HTTP integration and runtime identity.
Set request deadlines, downstream timeouts and response limits.
tests: Send valid and invalid requests and assert status and response schema.
Exercise authorization failure, duplicate submission and downstream timeout.
failures: 502: inspect integration response format and handler logs.
Timeout: compare gateway, runtime and downstream deadlines.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

title: Use CloudFront Origin Access Control for supported S3 origins
description: Edge request routing and origin access for Amazon CloudFront. Integration contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy. Control: Use CloudFront Origin Access Control for supported S3 origins.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_oac_enforced_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Origin Access Control (OAC) with SigV4 for S3 and ALB Origins
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.origin
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure origin.origin_access_control_id for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_viewer_protocol_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Security Policy and HTTPS Redirect on Viewers
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.viewer_certificate
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure viewer_certificate.minimum_protocol_version for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_waf_webacl_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach AWS WAF WebACL to CloudFront Distribution Edge
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.web_acl_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure web_acl_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_oac_enforced_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Origin Access Control (OAC) with SigV4 for S3 and ALB Origins (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.origin
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure origin.origin_access_control_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_viewer_protocol_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Security Policy and HTTPS Redirect on Viewers (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.viewer_certificate
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure viewer_certificate.minimum_protocol_version for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_waf_webacl_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach AWS WAF WebACL to CloudFront Distribution Edge (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.web_acl_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure web_acl_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_oac_enforced_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Origin Access Control (OAC) with SigV4 for S3 and ALB Origins (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.origin
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure origin.origin_access_control_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_viewer_protocol_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Security Policy and HTTPS Redirect on Viewers (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.viewer_certificate
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure viewer_certificate.minimum_protocol_version for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_waf_webacl_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach AWS WAF WebACL to CloudFront Distribution Edge (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.web_acl_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure web_acl_id for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_oac_enforced_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Origin Access Control (OAC) with SigV4 for S3 and ALB Origins (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.origin
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure origin.origin_access_control_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_viewer_protocol_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Security Policy and HTTPS Redirect on Viewers (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.viewer_certificate
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure viewer_certificate.minimum_protocol_version for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_waf_webacl_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach AWS WAF WebACL to CloudFront Distribution Edge (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.web_acl_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure web_acl_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_oac_enforced_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Origin Access Control (OAC) with SigV4 for S3 and ALB Origins (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.origin
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure origin.origin_access_control_id for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_viewer_protocol_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Security Policy and HTTPS Redirect on Viewers (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.viewer_certificate
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure viewer_certificate.minimum_protocol_version for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_waf_webacl_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Attach AWS WAF WebACL to CloudFront Distribution Edge (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.web_acl_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure web_acl_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_oac_enforced_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Origin Access Control (OAC) with SigV4 for S3 and ALB Origins (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.origin
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure origin.origin_access_control_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

opa_policy:
package aws.edge_cloudfront.edge_cloudfront_cloudfront_viewer_protocol_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce TLS 1.2+ Security Policy and HTTPS Redirect on Viewers (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudfront_distribution"
  not r.change.after.viewer_certificate
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure viewer_certificate.minimum_protocol_version for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
