developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_target_dlq_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure EventBridge Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Failed Target Invocations (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_target"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_kms_cmk_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption on Custom EventBridge Event Buses (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_identifier
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_identifier for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_bus_policy_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Strict Resource-Based Policies on Cross-Account Event Bus Routing (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.principal for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_target_dlq_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure EventBridge Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Failed Target Invocations (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_target"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_kms_cmk_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption on Custom EventBridge Event Buses (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_identifier
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_identifier for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_bus_policy_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Strict Resource-Based Policies on Cross-Account Event Bus Routing (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.principal for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

aws configure list

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_target_dlq_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure EventBridge Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Failed Target Invocations (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_target"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_kms_cmk_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption on Custom EventBridge Event Buses (Tier-10 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_identifier
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_identifier for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_bus_policy_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Strict Resource-Based Policies on Cross-Account Event Bus Routing (Tier-10 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.principal for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_target_dlq_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure EventBridge Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Failed Target Invocations (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_target"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_kms_cmk_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption on Custom EventBridge Event Buses (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_identifier
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_identifier for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_bus_policy_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Strict Resource-Based Policies on Cross-Account Event Bus Routing (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.principal for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_target_dlq_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure EventBridge Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Failed Target Invocations (Tier-11 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_target"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.arn for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_kms_cmk_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption on Custom EventBridge Event Buses (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_identifier
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_identifier for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_bus_policy_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Strict Resource-Based Policies on Cross-Account Event Bus Routing (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.principal for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_target_dlq_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure EventBridge Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Failed Target Invocations (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_target"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_kms_cmk_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption on Custom EventBridge Event Buses (Tier-13 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_identifier
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_identifier for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_bus_policy_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Strict Resource-Based Policies on Cross-Account Event Bus Routing (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.principal for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

aws configure list

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_target_dlq_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure EventBridge Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Failed Target Invocations (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_target"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_kms_cmk_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption on Custom EventBridge Event Buses (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_identifier
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_identifier for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_bus_policy_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Strict Resource-Based Policies on Cross-Account Event Bus Routing (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus_policy"
  not r.change.after.statement
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statement.principal for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_target_dlq_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure EventBridge Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) for Failed Target Invocations (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_target"
  not r.change.after.dead_letter_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dead_letter_config.arn for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.decoupled_eventbridge.decoupled_eventbridge_eventbridge_kms_cmk_t15

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer Managed KMS Encryption on Custom EventBridge Event Buses (Tier-15 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_cloudwatch_event_bus"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_identifier
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_identifier for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Asynchronous worker and dead-letter recovery
developer_guide.contract: Message ID, schema version, idempotency key, ack deadline and retry limit
dependencies: A producer, message channel and explicit consumer integration
A worker identity, retry policy and dead-letter destination
An idempotent write or side-effect handler
steps: Create the channel, subscription or queue and configure consumer permissions.
Implement idempotency and acknowledge only after successful processing.
Configure retry and dead-letter behavior and a controlled replay procedure.
tests: Send a valid message, a duplicate and a poison message.
Confirm successful side effects, bounded retries and dead-letter delivery.
failures: Message age rising: inspect consumer health, permissions and concurrency.
Duplicate writes: inspect idempotency storage and acknowledgement timing.

package aws.aiml_sagemaker.aiml_sagemaker_sagemaker_vpc_only_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce VPC Only Mode on SageMaker Studio to Prevent Direct Internet Access
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_sagemaker_domain"
  not r.change.after.app_network_access_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure app_network_access_type for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

opa_policy:
package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted

    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-7 • Profile S)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-7 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
