developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-10 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-10 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted

    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-11 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted

    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-13 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_region_restriction_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Restricting Permitted AWS Regions to Avoid Sprawl (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.condition.string_not_equals.aws_requested_region for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_protect_security_services_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Disabling of GuardDuty and CloudTrail (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.effect for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package aws.governance_org.governance_org_org_scp_deny_leave_t15

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Service Control Policy (SCP) Denying Leaving AWS Organization (Tier-15 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_organizations_policy"
  not r.change.after.content
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure content.action for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.

Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

opa_policy:
package aws.dns_route53.dns_route53_route53_dnssec_enabled_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable DNSSEC Signing on Route 53 Hosted Zones with KMS Key-Signing Key
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_route53_key_signing_key"
  not r.change.after.status
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure status for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

opa_policy:
package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_kms_cmk_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.encrypt_at_rest
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypt_at_rest.kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_vpc_subnets_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Private VPC Subnet Placement with Fine-Grained Access Control
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.vpc_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_options.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_node_to_node_tls_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Node-to-Node TLS Encryption on OpenSearch Cluster Domains (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.node_to_node_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure node_to_node_encryption.enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_kms_cmk_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.encrypt_at_rest
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypt_at_rest.kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.

Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

opa_policy:
package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_vpc_subnets_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Private VPC Subnet Placement with Fine-Grained Access Control (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.vpc_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_options.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_node_to_node_tls_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Node-to-Node TLS Encryption on OpenSearch Cluster Domains (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.node_to_node_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure node_to_node_encryption.enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_kms_cmk_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.encrypt_at_rest
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypt_at_rest.kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

opa_policy:
package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_vpc_subnets_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Private VPC Subnet Placement with Fine-Grained Access Control (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.vpc_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_options.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_node_to_node_tls_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Node-to-Node TLS Encryption on OpenSearch Cluster Domains (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.node_to_node_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure node_to_node_encryption.enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_kms_cmk_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.encrypt_at_rest
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypt_at_rest.kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["AWS: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Amazon OpenSearch"]
      requirement["Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-1000"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:analytics-opensearch", label: "Amazon OpenSearch", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_vpc_subnets_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Private VPC Subnet Placement with Fine-Grained Access Control (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.vpc_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_options.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_node_to_node_tls_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Node-to-Node TLS Encryption on OpenSearch Cluster Domains (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.node_to_node_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure node_to_node_encryption.enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_kms_cmk_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.encrypt_at_rest
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypt_at_rest.kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_vpc_subnets_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Private VPC Subnet Placement with Fine-Grained Access Control (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.vpc_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_options.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["AWS: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Amazon OpenSearch"]
      requirement["Enforce Private VPC Subnet Placement with Fine-Grained Access Control"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:iam-access", label: "IAM authorization for this action", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: AWS-BP-1004"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["AWS: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:analytics-opensearch", label: "Amazon OpenSearch", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_node_to_node_tls_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Node-to-Node TLS Encryption on OpenSearch Cluster Domains (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 1.4, SOC 2 CC6.8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.node_to_node_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure node_to_node_encryption.enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_kms_cmk_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce KMS Customer Managed Key Storage Encryption at Rest (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.encrypt_at_rest
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure encrypt_at_rest.kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_vpc_subnets_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Private VPC Subnet Placement with Fine-Grained Access Control (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 2.1.1, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP Moderate
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.vpc_options
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_options.subnet_ids for compliance standard CIS AWS 2.1.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package aws.analytics_opensearch.analytics_opensearch_opensearch_node_to_node_tls_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Node-to-Node TLS Encryption on OpenSearch Cluster Domains (Tier-7 • Profile S)
# Compliance: CIS AWS 3.1.4, ISO 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_opensearch_domain"
  not r.change.after.node_to_node_encryption
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure node_to_node_encryption.enabled for compliance standard CIS AWS 3.1.4", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in AWS Console or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

    end

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:logging-cloudtrail", label: "Supported CloudTrail management events", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
